ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular superconducting loop located above an infinitely long straight wire below. The long side of the rectangular loop is labeled ℓ, and the vertical width is labeled w; the distance from the lower side of the loop to the infinitely long straight wire is labeled d. In the figure, the loop current I1 is counterclockwise: the current in the lower horizontal side is to the right, and the current in the upper horizontal side is to the left. The current direction of the long straight wire below is not drawn. Reasoning: In order to produce an attractive force between the long straight wire and the rectangular loop, take the current I2 in the long straight wire to be in the same direction as the current in the lower horizontal side of the rectangular loop, namely to the right. It is known that ℓ=200 cm=2.00 m, w=2 cm=0.020 m, d=1 cm=0.010 m, r=0.5 mm=5.0×10^-4 m, and the initial superconducting current I1=5 A. The magnetic flux of the superconducting loop is conserved, and according to the specified approximation it is written as L I + M I2 = L I1, therefore the final loop current I = I1 - (M/L)I2. The mutual inductance of the long straight wire and the rectangular loop is approximated as M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d). The self-inductance of the loop is approximated as the self-inductance form of two long parallel wires: L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r). Substituting numerical values: M = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / 2π) ln(0.030/0.010) = 4.394×10^-7 H. L = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / π) ln(0.020/0.0005) = 2.951×10^-6 H. Neglecting the magnetic field of the vertical sides, the resultant force on the horizontal sides is F = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) I I2 [1/d - 1/(d+w)]. Substituting I = I1 - (M/L)I2, it can be known that F is a quadratic function of I2, and is maximum when I2 = L I1/(2M). At this time I = I1/2. Therefore Fmax = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)] × L I1^2/(4M). The numerical value is Fmax = (4π×10^-7×2.00/2π)(100 - 33.333...) × (2.951×10^-6 × 25)/(4×4.394×10^-7) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N.

raw_record.question_text:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the rectangular superconducting loop lies above a long straight wire; the lower horizontal side of the loop is a distance d from the long wire, the upper side is at distance d+w, and the loop current shown is counterclockwise so the lower side carries current to the right and the upper side to the left. Choose the long-wire current direction so it is parallel to the lower side, giving attraction. From the text take ℓ=2.00 m, w=0.020 m, d=0.010 m, r=5.0e-4 m, and initial superconducting current I1=5 A. Neglect vertical sides as instructed. Use flux conservation in a superconducting loop: L I + M I2 = L I1, where I is the final loop current. Use the long-wire field to compute mutual inductance M = (μ0 ℓ/2π) ln((d+w)/d). Approximate the loop self-inductance as two long parallel wires separated by w: L ≈ (μ0 ℓ/π) ln(w/r). Then I = I1 - (M/L)I2. Compute the net attractive force from the two horizontal sides using wire-wire force per length: F = (μ0 ℓ/2π) I I2 [1/d - 1/(d+w)]. This is a quadratic in I2, maximize it at I2 = L I1/(2M), giving Fmax = (μ0 ℓ/2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)] L I1^2/(4M). Substitute the values to obtain about 1.12e-3 N.

图像描述：图中有一个位于下方无限长直导线之上的矩形超导回路。矩形回路的长边标为 ℓ，竖直宽度标为 w；回路下边到无限长直导线的距离标为 d。图中回路电流 I1 为逆时针方向：下水平边电流向右，上水平边电流向左。下方长直导线未画出电流方向。

推理：为了使长直导线与矩形回路之间产生吸引力，取长直导线电流 I2 与矩形回路下水平边电流同向，即向右。已知 ℓ=200 cm=2.00 m，w=2 cm=0.020 m，d=1 cm=0.010 m，r=0.5 mm=5.0×10^-4 m，初始超导电流 I1=5 A。

超导回路磁通守恒，按指定近似写为 L I + M I2 = L I1，因此最终回路电流 I = I1 - (M/L)I2。

长直导线与矩形回路的互感近似为 M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d)。回路自感近似为两根长平行导线的自感形式：L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r)。

代入数值：M = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / 2π) ln(0.030/0.010) = 4.394×10^-7 H。L = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / π) ln(0.020/0.0005) = 2.951×10^-6 H。

忽略竖直边磁场，水平边受力合力为 F = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) I I2 [1/d - 1/(d+w)]。代入 I = I1 - (M/L)I2，可知 F 是关于 I2 的二次函数，在 I2 = L I1/(2M) 时最大。此时 I = I1/2。

所以 Fmax = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)] × L I1^2/(4M)。数值为 Fmax = (4π×10^-7×2.00/2π)(100 - 33.333...) × (2.951×10^-6 × 25)/(4×4.394×10^-7) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N。

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the long wire is below the rectangular loop; the diagram shows the loop’s lower and upper horizontal sides parallel to the long wire, separated from it by d and d+w respectively, with loop current clockwise/counterclockwise orientation as drawn so the bottom segment is the side that can be made attractive by choosing the long-wire current in the same direction. From the text use ℓ=2.00 m, w=0.020 m, d=0.010 m, r=0.0005 m, I1=5 A. Model the system with an inductance matrix instead of summing segment forces. The loop has self-inductance L ≈ (μ0ℓ/π)ln(w/r). The mutual inductance between the long wire and the loop depends on separation d: M(d) = (μ0ℓ/2π)ln((d+w)/d). Superconducting flux conservation gives L I + M(d) I2 = L I1, so I = I1 - M I2/L. Use magnetic coenergy to get the attractive force magnitude at fixed currents: F = |I I2 dM/dd| = I I2 (μ0ℓ/2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w)). Substitute the flux-conservation expression for I, maximize I2(I1 - MI2/L), and evaluate at I2 = L I1/(2M). This gives the same numerical maximum, 1.12e-3 N.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有一个细长矩形 superconducting loop 位于一根无限长水平直导线的上方。矩形环的下边与长直导线平行，二者间距标为 d；矩形环的上边与长直导线距离为 d+w。矩形环水平长度标为 ℓ，竖直宽度标为 w。图中环电流 I1 沿左边向下、下边向右、右边向上、上边向左，即逆时针方向。长直导线在环下方水平延伸。

再推理：按指定方法，用电感矩阵处理超导环的磁通守恒。已知 ℓ=200 cm=2.00 m，w=2 cm=0.020 m，d=1 cm=0.010 m，r=0.5 mm=0.0005 m，I1=5 A。近似取矩形环自感 L ≈ (μ0 ℓ/π) ln(w/r)。因此 L = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / π) ln(0.020/0.0005) = 8.0×10^-7 ln(40) ≈ 2.951×10^-6 H。长直导线与矩形环的互感 M(d) = (μ0 ℓ/2π) ln((d+w)/d)。所以 M = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / 2π) ln(0.030/0.010) = 4.0×10^-7 ln(3) ≈ 4.394×10^-7 H。

超导环总磁通守恒：L I + M I2 = L I1，因此 I = I1 - (M/L) I2。若长直导线电流方向选为与环下边电流相同，则下边与长直导线相吸；上边反向而相斥，但距离更远，净力可为吸引。由磁共能，固定电流时吸引力大小为 F = |I I2 dM/dd| = I I2 (μ0 ℓ/2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w))。令 K = (μ0 ℓ/2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w))，则 K = 4.0×10^-7(100 - 33.3333) ≈ 2.667×10^-5。

代入 I = I1 - (M/L)I2，得到 F = K I2(I1 - M I2/L)。这是关于 I2 的二次函数，最大值在 I2 = L I1/(2M) 处取得。最大时 I = I1/2。于是 Fmax = K L I1^2/(4M)。数值为 Fmax = (2.667×10^-5)(2.951×10^-6)(25)/(4×4.394×10^-7) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N。

method.CoT_final:
先描述图像：图中有一个细长矩形 superconducting loop 位于一根无限长水平直导线的上方。矩形环的下边与长直导线平行，二者间距标为 d；矩形环的上边与长直导线距离为 d+w。矩形环水平长度标为 ℓ，竖直宽度标为 w。图中环电流 I1 沿左边向下、下边向右、右边向上、上边向左，即逆时针方向。长直导线在环下方水平延伸。

再推理：按指定方法，用电感矩阵处理超导环的磁通守恒。已知 ℓ=200 cm=2.00 m，w=2 cm=0.020 m，d=1 cm=0.010 m，r=0.5 mm=0.0005 m，I1=5 A。近似取矩形环自感 L ≈ (μ0 ℓ/π) ln(w/r)。因此 L = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / π) ln(0.020/0.0005) = 8.0×10^-7 ln(40) ≈ 2.951×10^-6 H。长直导线与矩形环的互感 M(d) = (μ0 ℓ/2π) ln((d+w)/d)。所以 M = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / 2π) ln(0.030/0.010) = 4.0×10^-7 ln(3) ≈ 4.394×10^-7 H。

超导环总磁通守恒：L I + M I2 = L I1，因此 I = I1 - (M/L) I2。若长直导线电流方向选为与环下边电流相同，则下边与长直导线相吸；上边反向而相斥，但距离更远，净力可为吸引。由磁共能，固定电流时吸引力大小为 F = |I I2 dM/dd| = I I2 (μ0 ℓ/2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w))。令 K = (μ0 ℓ/2π)(1/d - 1/(d+w))，则 K = 4.0×10^-7(100 - 33.3333) ≈ 2.667×10^-5。

代入 I = I1 - (M/L)I2，得到 F = K I2(I1 - M I2/L)。这是关于 I2 的二次函数，最大值在 I2 = L I1/(2M) 处取得。最大时 I = I1/2。于是 Fmax = K L I1^2/(4M)。数值为 Fmax = (2.667×10^-5)(2.951×10^-6)(25)/(4×4.394×10^-7) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route obtains the force from the derivative of the mutual inductance/coenergy with respect to separation, rather than from explicit pairwise forces on the two horizontal loop segments. It is therefore a different executable reasoning path though it uses the same superconducting constraint.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image identifies which distances enter M(d): the rectangular loop spans from d to d+w above the long wire, has horizontal length ℓ, and the relevant parallel portions are the top and bottom sides of the loop.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text provides all numerical parameters, the initial current, the fact that the loop is superconducting, and the hint justifying omission of vertical-segment contributions.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Uses inductance-matrix modeling, flux conservation in a superconducting loop, mutual inductance of a rectangular loop with a long straight wire, coenergy force formula F = |I1 I2 dM/dd|, approximate two-wire self-inductance, and optimization of a concave quadratic.

raw_record.original_question:
Consider a rectangular loop made of superconducting material with length $\ell=200 \mathrm{~cm}$ and width $w=2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The radius of this particular wire is $r=0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. This superconducting rectangular loop initially has a current $I_{1}=5 \mathrm{~A}$ in the counterclockwise direction as shown in the figure below. This rectangular loop is situated a distance $d=1 \mathrm{~cm}$ above an infinitely long wire that initially contains no current. Suppose that the current in the infinitely long wire is increased to some current $I_{2}$ such that there is an attractive force $F$ between the rectangular loop and the long wire. Find the maximum possible value of $F$. Write your answer in newtons.
Hint: You may neglect the magnetic field produced by the vertical segments in the rectangular loop.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular superconducting loop located above an infinitely long straight wire below. The long side of the rectangular loop is labeled ℓ, and the vertical width is labeled w; the distance from the lower side of the loop to the infinitely long straight wire is labeled d. In the figure, the loop current I1 is counterclockwise: the current in the lower horizontal side is to the right, and the current in the upper horizontal side is to the left. The current direction of the long straight wire below is not drawn.

Reasoning: In order to produce an attractive force between the long straight wire and the rectangular loop, take the current I2 in the long straight wire to be in the same direction as the current in the lower horizontal side of the rectangular loop, namely to the right. It is known that ℓ=200 cm=2.00 m, w=2 cm=0.020 m, d=1 cm=0.010 m, r=0.5 mm=5.0×10^-4 m, and the initial superconducting current I1=5 A.

The magnetic flux of the superconducting loop is conserved, and according to the specified approximation it is written as L I + M I2 = L I1, therefore the final loop current I = I1 - (M/L)I2.

The mutual inductance of the long straight wire and the rectangular loop is approximated as M = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) ln((d+w)/d). The self-inductance of the loop is approximated as the self-inductance form of two long parallel wires: L ≈ (μ0 ℓ / π) ln(w/r).

Substituting numerical values: M = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / 2π) ln(0.030/0.010) = 4.394×10^-7 H. L = (4π×10^-7 × 2.00 / π) ln(0.020/0.0005) = 2.951×10^-6 H.

Neglecting the magnetic field of the vertical sides, the resultant force on the horizontal sides is F = (μ0 ℓ / 2π) I I2 [1/d - 1/(d+w)]. Substituting I = I1 - (M/L)I2, it can be known that F is a quadratic function of I2, and is maximum when I2 = L I1/(2M). At this time I = I1/2.

Therefore Fmax = (μ0 ℓ / 2π)[1/d - 1/(d+w)] × L I1^2/(4M). The numerical value is Fmax = (4π×10^-7×2.00/2π)(100 - 33.333...) × (2.951×10^-6 × 25)/(4×4.394×10^-7) ≈ 1.12×10^-3 N.
